questions.q: Group-<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn></math> elements react with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in amorphous form to form oxides of type <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo>=</mo></math> element). Which among the following is the most basic oxide?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The basicity of an oxide is closely related to the electropositive character of the element. The more electropositive the element, the more basic its oxide will be. This is because the oxide ion can react with a cation to form a basic oxide. As we move down Group 13, the electropositive character of the elements increases, and so does the basicity of their oxides.

B2O3<Al2O3<Ga2O3<In2O3<Tl2O3

So most basic oxide among the given options is Tl2O3.

questions.q:
The property/properties that show irregularity in first four elements of group-17 is/are :
(A) Covalent radius
(B) Electron affinity
(C) Ionic radius
(D) First ionization energy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The order of first four elements of group-17 are as follows.
\(\mathrm{F} \lt \mathrm{Cl} \lt \mathrm{Br} \lt \mathrm{I}\) (Covalent radius)
\(\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{I}\) (Electron affinity)
\(\mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Br}^{-} \lt \mathrm{I}^{-}\)(Ionic radius)
\(\mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{I}\left(\mathrm{I}^{\text {st }}\right.\) ionization energy\)
Electron affinity order is irregular.

A. The properties of elements are function of atomic weights.
B. The properties of elements are function of atomic numbers.
C. Elements having similar outer electronic configurations are arranged in same period.
D. An element's location reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital.

questions.q: In general, the properties that decrease and increase down a group in the periodic table, respectively, are :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
(i) Electronegativity: Top to bottom decrease.

(ii) Atomic Radius: generally Increases top to Bottom.

(iii) Electron affinity: generally top to bottom decreases.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution: Catenation is the tendency to link with one another through covalent bonds to form chain and rings, i.e., catenation. This is because bonds are very strong in the carbon family. questions.q: The CORRECT order of first ionisation enthalpy is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The ionization energy of the elements increases from left to right in the periodic table. The first ionization of magnesium is greater than that of aluminium because magnesium has a stable complete electronic configuration 1s22s22p63s2, so it requires more energy to remove the first electron from it, whereas aluminium has electronic configuration 1s22s22p63s23p1 which need lesser energy than that of magnesium. Similarly, phosphorus has more ionisation energy than sulphur due to the half filled electronic configuration in the phosphorus.

 Mg  Al  P S→IE .order ⇒Al<Mg<S<P

options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
Mg have 2 electrons in valance shell and after donation of 2 electrons it converts into Mg2+ ion and attains inert gas configuration, now to ionize one more electron from inert gas configuration is very difficult, hence it is easy to ionize Mg to Mg2+. IE2 is always greater than IE1 because on removal of e-, size decreases and effective nuclear charge increases.So Assertion is correct.

Mg2+ is a smaller ion than Mg+ and has a greater charge density. This means that Mg2+ has a stronger attraction to its electrons than Mg+ and requires more energy to remove an electron from it. So reason is also correct.

questions.q: . Identify the correct order of standard enthalpy of formation of sodium halides.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
The lattice energy of an ionic compound is the energy required to separate one mole of the compound into its constituent ions in the gas phase.

 Lattice energy∝1r++r-

The lattice energy is inversely proportional to the sum of the ionic radii r++r- of the ions involved. When the size of the ions increases, the distance between them also increases, leading to a decrease in the attractive forces between the ions and a decrease in the lattice energy. Therefore, if the size of the ions increases, the lattice energy generally decreases.

So Order : NaF > NaCl > NaBr > NaI

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases down the group from Li to Cs. This is because of increase in size which outweighs the increasing nuclear charge, and the outermost electron is very well screened from the nuclear charge.

Li>Na>K

Due to stable electronic configuration noble gases exhibit very high ionisation enthalpy. However, it decreases down the group with increase in atomic size.

He>Ne>Ar>Kr>Xe>Rn

Alkaline earths have higher ionization enthalpy values than alkali metals. This is because the atomic size of alkaline earths is smaller than that of alkali metals.

Sr>Rb

Because of completely filled configuration, zinc is stable and requires higher ionization energy whereas gallium is yet to fill its p-orbitals, so it has lower ionization energy compared to zinc.

Zn>Ga

questions.q:
Which of the following statements are not correct?

A. The electron gain enthalpy of F is more negative than that of Cl.

B. Ionization enthalpy decreases in a group of periodic table.

C. The electronegativity of an atom depends upon the atoms bonded to it.

D. Al2O3 and NO are examples of amphoteric oxides.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
A is incorrect. F and Cl belong to the same group of the periodic table. The electron gain enthalpy usually becomes less negative on moving down a group. However, in this case, the value of the electron gain enthalpy of Cl is more negative than that of F. This is because the atomic size of F is smaller than that of Cl. 

B is correct (ionisation energy decreases down the group).

C is incorrect (Electronegativity is a fixed property of an element and is typically measured on scales such as the Pauling scale or the Mulliken scale.). 

D is incorrect. The oxides which behave as both acidic and basic oxides are called amphoteric oxides. . Here Al2O3 is amphoteric oxide and NO is neutral oxide.

Hence, A, C and D are incorrect.

questions.q: The correct order of ionic size of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>Na</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo>-</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>Mg</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is :

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution:
These are all isoelectronic species. More the negative charge on the species, more is the size of that ion and more the positive charge on the species, less is the size of that ion.

The correct order of ionic radii isN-3>O-2>F->Na+>Mg+2Radii

(Isoelectronic species)
